note: Tuesday 20 Oct 2026, 07:02 SGT run, before Asia's open. Monday 19 Oct's US close confirmed a broad, genuine rebound from Friday's AI-credit-stress selloff: S&P 500 +0.41% to 7690.73, Nasdaq +1.11% to 26430.89, Dow -0.07% to 51966.03, Russell 2000 +0.25%, VIX -7.75% to 18.44. CNN's Fear & Greed could not be fetched directly (403/451) but was corroborated across 3 independent mirrors converging on 24/Extreme Fear for Monday (up slightly from Friday's 18), with crypto Fear & Greed at 59/Greed via alternative.me. Breadth stayed narrower than the index-level bounce implied: NYSE decliners (1,761) still outnumbered advancers (945) on Monday despite the S&P's gain, new highs/lows and the McClellan Summation Index (-991.5) remained deeply negative, and only 3 of 11 GICS sectors (Tech, Energy, Health Care) have a majority of members above their 200-DMA -- a textbook narrow, AI/megacap-driven rally rather than a broad one. Fund flows: the latest full BofA/EPFR Flow Show edition (week ended Oct 14) is still the newest available (next due ~Oct 21-23); it shows cash outflows (-$53.1B) funding equity inflows (+$39.1B, led by large-cap tech) and a 16th straight weekly Treasury inflow, a window that entirely predates Thursday/Friday's AI-credit scare. Freshest narrower data points (HK Southbound Connect flipping to -HK$6.6bn net selling, GLD-specific ETF outflows of ~$727M) suggest some of that risk appetite was already cooling into the weekend.

flows.period: week ending Wed Oct 14, 2026 (BofA Flow Show / EPFR) -- next edition (w/e ~Oct 21) not yet published
flows.narrative: The latest BofA/EPFR Flow Show (week ended Oct 14) showed a classic late-cycle rotation: investors pulled $53.1B from cash while pushing $39.1B into US equities and extending Treasury inflows to a 16th straight week, even as the Oct 16 AI-infrastructure-credit scare was just beginning. Europe equity funds saw continued outflows (-$1.5B) while EM/China attracted fresh money (+$17.7B/+$8.6B); gold and crypto flows were roughly flat in the fund-flow data. Fresher, narrower data points -- HK Southbound Connect flipping to net selling and GLD-specific outflows into Oct 16 -- suggest some of that risk appetite cooled heading into the weekend selloff.
